title: Audit Export Config API (Draft Notes) — CRUD, validation, filters, migration
content:
Owner: Benji (Platform Eng)
Last updated: 2025-04-05
Status: Draft notes / API shape proposals for SIEM-ready audit export beta (hosted + dedicated).

Goal
- Provide a control-plane API to manage “audit export configurations” per tenant/workspace.
- Support: destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3), credentials via secret references, filter model, backfill window, and operational status/health surface.
- Must be feature-flagged + allowlisted per tenant for beta.

Non-goals (beta)
- Private/on-prem full support (documented follow-on).
- Exact-once delivery guarantee; we are at-least-once (downstream dedup required).
- Arbitrary transforms (e.g., custom field mapping beyond destination adapter defaults).

Key constraints / requirements
- RBAC: least-privilege. Separate permissions for read vs manage vs rotate credentials.
- Validation: strong validation at create/update time; fail closed.
- Secrets: no raw secrets in request/response after creation; prefer secret refs (Vault/KMS-backed).
- Tenant isolation: all resources are tenant-scoped; no cross-tenant leakage.
- Auditing: changes to export configs are themselves audit logged (who changed what).

Terminology (draft)
- tenant_id: Redwood tenant/account id (global)
- workspace_id: workspace/project id (within tenant) — export configs are workspace-scoped unless we decide tenant-scoped exports.
  - Current leaning: workspace-scoped; allow an optional “all workspaces” later.
- export_config: a named configuration describing destination + filters + schedule semantics.
- destination: type + settings (splunk/datadog/s3)
- secret_ref: pointer to stored credentials (HEC token, API key, IAM role/keys)
- checkpoint: exporter-side delivery checkpoint (NOT stored/managed via this API; status endpoint surfaces derived summary)

API versioning
- Propose /v1 for beta with fields marked “beta” as needed.
- Backwards compatibility within v1: additive-only; do not rename fields.

Resource model
- ExportConfig is primary resource.
- We also need an action endpoint for “test connection” (best-effort) and “rotate secret ref” (or generic update).
- Health/status is read-only; computed from exporter metrics/checkpoints.

Base URL
- /control-plane/v1

Endpoints (draft)

1) List export configs
GET /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports

Query params:
- include_disabled=(true|false) default true
- destination_type=splunk|datadog|s3 (optional)

Response: 200
{
  "items": [ExportConfigSummary],
  "next_cursor": "..." (optional)
}

ExportConfigSummary (draft)
- id, name, enabled
- destination_type
- created_at, updated_at
- last_delivery_at (optional)
- last_success_at (optional)
- last_error_code (optional; sanitized)
- export_lag_seconds (optional; best-effort)

NOTE: For list views, avoid returning destination credentials. Return destination settings that are non-sensitive (e.g., s3 bucket + prefix) + redacted token refs.


2) Get one export config
GET /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}

Response: 200 ExportConfig


3) Create export config
POST /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports

Request body: CreateExportConfigRequest
{
  "name": "splunk-prod",
  "enabled": true,
  "destination": DestinationSpec,
  "filter": FilterSpec,
  "backfill": BackfillSpec,
  "delivery": DeliverySpec,
  "labels": {"env":"prod","owner":"secops"} (optional)
}

Response: 201 ExportConfig

Idempotency:
- Suggest supporting Idempotency-Key header (optional but nice).
- Without header, client retries may create duplicates; we can mitigate with uniqueness constraints on (workspace_id, name).


4) Update export config (replace-ish)
PUT /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}

Request body: UpdateExportConfigRequest
- Same shape as create, but all fields optional? or require full replacement?

Open question: PATCH vs PUT
- I lean PATCH for partial updates, but many Redwood APIs use PUT. For beta: implement PATCH to reduce risk of clients clobbering fields.


5) Partial update
PATCH /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}

Request body examples:
- {"enabled": false}
- {"filter": {...}}
- {"destination": {...}} (validated)

Response: 200 ExportConfig


6) Delete export config
DELETE /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}

Behavior:
- Hard delete vs soft delete?
  - Beta: prefer soft delete with tombstone for 30d so exporter can drain/stop gracefully + audit trails are intact.
  - API can behave like delete but we keep internal record.

Response: 204


7) Test destination connectivity (best-effort)
POST /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}:test

Response: 200
{
  "ok": true|false,
  "checked_at": "...",
  "details": "human-readable summary",
  "error_code": "DEST_AUTH_FAILED" | "DEST_TIMEOUT" | "DEST_RATE_LIMIT" | "DEST_DNS" | ...,
  "recommendation": "..." (optional)
}

Notes:
- Do not leak sensitive headers, tokens, endpoint urls beyond what’s already configured.
- For Splunk/Datadog we can do a lightweight validation call; for S3 we can attempt PutObject to a test prefix (or HeadBucket + KMS perms check).


8) Get export status/health (read-only)
GET /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}/status

Response: 200 ExportStatus
{
  "state": "RUNNING"|"PAUSED"|"ERROR"|"DISABLED",
  "export_lag_seconds": 123,
  "last_success_at": "...",
  "last_attempt_at": "...",
  "last_error": {
    "code": "DEST_403"|"DEST_429"|"CHECKPOINT_WRITE_FAILED"|..., 
    "message": "sanitized short msg",
    "seen_at": "..."
  },
  "counters_24h": {
    "events_exported": 12345,
    "batches_failed": 12,
    "retries": 301
  }
}

Implementation note:
- Status is computed from exporter metrics/checkpoints and cached in control plane (to keep exporter isolated + avoid fanout).
- Cardinality concerns: counters should be coarse. Avoid per-error-instance payload.


9) Pause/resume (optional)
POST /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}:pause
POST /control-plane/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-exports/{export_config_id}:resume

Could be done via PATCH enabled=false, but pause/resume is distinct from disabled:
- disabled = customer-intended off
- paused = system safety (backpressure/max lag) or operator action (SRE)

Beta decision: keep it simple; use enabled toggle + exporter may auto-pause for safety and reflect in status only.


Data shapes (draft)

ExportConfig
{
  "id": "aex_...",
  "workspace_id": "w_...",
  "name": "splunk-prod",
  "enabled": true,
  "destination": DestinationSpec,
  "filter": FilterSpec,
  "backfill": BackfillSpec,
  "delivery": DeliverySpec,
  "created_at": "2025-03-12T18:21:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2025-04-05T10:08:31Z",
  "created_by": {"actor_id":"u_...","type":"user"},
  "updated_by": {"actor_id":"u_...","type":"user"}
}

created_by/updated_by:
- Must align with audit event schema v2 actor fields; at minimum include actor_id + actor_type. Avoid emails.

DestinationSpec (tagged union)
{
  "type": "splunk",
  "splunk": { ... }
}
OR
{
  "type": "datadog",
  "datadog": { ... }
}
OR
{
  "type": "s3",
  "s3": { ... }
}

SplunkDestination (draft)
{
  "endpoint": "https://http-inputs-<host>:8088",
  "hec_token_ref": "secret://...",
  "index": "main" (optional),
  "source": "redwood" (optional),
  "sourcetype": "redwood:audit" (optional),
  "tls": {"verify": true} (default true),
  "batch": {"max_events": 500, "max_bytes": 512000} (optional)
}

Validation notes:
- endpoint host must be allowlisted (see ENG-5189 egress controls); reject RFC1918 unless explicitly allowed for Dedicated? (Open question.)
- endpoint must be https.
- hec_token_ref must reference a secret in the same workspace/tenant scope.

DatadogDestination (draft)
{
  "site": "datadoghq.com" | "datadoghq.eu" | "us3.datadoghq.com" (TBD),
  "api_key_ref": "secret://...",
  "service": "redwood-audit" (default),
  "tags": ["env:prod","team:secops"] (optional),
  "batch": {"max_events": 1000, "max_bytes": 512000} (optional)
}

Validation notes:
- Ensure api key scope supports logs intake (support ticket SUP-18497 suggests key scoping pitfalls).
- site must be one of supported values (no arbitrary hostnames in beta).

S3Destination (draft)
{
  "bucket": "customer-audit-logs",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "prefix": "redwood/audit/",
  "format": "jsonl_gzip" (beta),
  "partitioning": "dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH" (implementation-defined),
  "encryption": {
    "type": "SSE_S3"|"SSE_KMS",
    "kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:..." (required if SSE_KMS)
  },
  "auth": {
    "mode": "assume_role",
    "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/RedwoodAuditExportRole",
    "external_id_ref": "secret://..." (optional)
  }
}

Validation notes:
- bucket name syntax.
- region must match allowed deployment regions for the tenant (residency).
- If assume_role: role_arn required; disallow access keys for beta? (Open question; SRE testing matrix includes both.)
- If kms: kms_key_arn required.

Secret handling
- Request may include secret refs only (preferred), not raw tokens.
- If product insists on supporting “inline secret create” in Console, propose a separate endpoint:
  - POST /secrets {type, value} returns secret_ref
  - then POST /audit-exports uses secret_ref
- Ensure all responses return only secret_ref + metadata (created_at), never secret values.

FilterSpec (draft)

We need a model that is:
- Expressive enough for security ops (categories/actions, actor/resource)
- Safe (PII minimization; no arbitrary substring matches on payload)
- Efficient to evaluate (control plane validates; exporter evaluates).

Proposal (align ADR: allowlist/denylist + predicates)
{
  "mode": "ALLOW" | "DENY",  
  "categories": ["auth","admin","billing","inference","apikey","rbac","workspace"],
  "actions": ["apikey.create","apikey.delete"] (optional),
  "resource": {
    "types": ["api_key","workspace","model_deployment"] (optional),
    "ids": ["...","..."] (optional)
  },
  "actor": {
    "types": ["user","service_account"],
    "ids": ["u_...","sa_..."]
  },
  "include_system": false (default false)
}

Interpretation:
- mode=ALLOW: only events matching predicates are exported.
- mode=DENY: everything exported EXCEPT those matching predicates.

Defaults (beta)
- If filter omitted: export ALL categories (except include_system=false).
- include_system=false means internal Redwood operator actions not initiated by the customer are excluded by default. (Needs Security alignment.)

Validation rules:
- categories must be from canonical taxonomy (audit schema v2).
- actions must be from known set OR allow “prefix.*”? (Open question. Better to allow exact list only for beta.)
- resource.ids and actor.ids must be <= N (to avoid huge configs). Suggest max 100 each.

BackfillSpec (draft)
{
  "on_create": {"enabled": true, "window_hours": 24},
  "on_update": {"enabled": false}
}

Notes:
- Backfill is sensitive: interacts with retention policy and can create event volume spikes.
- Beta default: on_create enabled with 24h, max 168h (7d) hard limit.
- If a customer requests more: manual support workflow + Security approval.

DeliverySpec (draft)
{
  "delivery_guarantee": "AT_LEAST_ONCE",
  "max_lag_seconds": 86400 (optional; exporter safety threshold),
  "retry_policy": {"type":"exponential","max_attempts": 0 (means infinite),"max_backoff_seconds": 900}
}

Note: delivery policy may be exporter-only; control plane stores config but exporter enforces.

RBAC / Permissions (draft)
- audit_exports.read
  - list/get/status
- audit_exports.write
  - create/update/delete, enable/disable
- audit_exports.test
  - run :test (could be included in write)
- secrets.read_ref
  - ability to attach an existing secret_ref to destination
- secrets.write
  - create/rotate secret values (separate from audit export permission)

Roles (defaults; see policy bundle PR)
- Workspace Admin: read/write/test
- Security Auditor: read/status only
- Billing Admin: no by default

Feature flags / rollout controls
- require feature flag: feature.siem_audit_export_beta
- require tenant allowlist (admin tool) for create/update endpoints; non-allowlisted tenants get 404 (preferred) or 403? (lean 404 to reduce “beta discovery”)
- status endpoint should also be gated (avoid leaking that feature exists)

Migration plan (existing audit consumers)
- There is no existing export config API. Migration concerns are:
  1) schema evolution for audit events (event_id, category) — needed first.
  2) config storage/migrations as we iterate API shape.

Plan:
- Phase 0 (internal only): DB tables + internal endpoints; exporter pulls configs from control plane.
- Phase 1 (beta API): expose v1 endpoints behind feature flag + allowlist.
- Phase 2 (GA): remove allowlist requirement; maintain kill switch. Provide Terraform module updates.

Data storage (rough)
- table audit_export_configs
  - id, workspace_id, name, enabled, destination_json, filter_json, backfill_json, delivery_json
  - created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
  - created_by, updated_by
- table audit_export_config_audit (optional)
  - config_id, changed_at, actor, diff summary

Open question: store destination_json encrypted at rest?
- Yes for secret refs? But refs are not secrets. Still may contain endpoint/bucket which is not super sensitive but is customer infra. Recommend encrypt the entire destination_json as a defense-in-depth measure (KMS envelope).

Validation rules (summary)
- Name uniqueness: (workspace_id, name) unique; max length 64; [a-z0-9-] recommended.
- Destination:
  - splunk endpoint https required; host allowlist check
  - datadog site must be enumerated
  - s3: bucket/prefix required; encryption required (SSE_S3 ok for beta; SSE_KMS recommended)
- Secret refs:
  - must exist; must be in same tenant/workspace scope
  - must be correct type (hec_token vs dd_api_key vs aws_external_id)
- Filters:
  - categories from taxonomy; enforce max array sizes
  - deny mode cannot specify empty predicate? (If mode=DENY and no predicates, it becomes “deny nothing” which is ok but confusing; maybe reject.)
- Backfill:
  - window_hours <= retention window (policy); hard limit 168h
  - backfill on update disabled by default

Errors (draft)
Standard error envelope:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED"|"FORBIDDEN"|"NOT_FOUND"|"CONFLICT"|"BETA_NOT_ENABLED",
    "message": "...",
    "field_errors": ["destination.splunk.endpoint must be https", ...]
  }
}

Observability hooks (for control plane)
- Metrics:
  - audit_export_config_create_total{result}
  - audit_export_config_update_total{result}
  - audit_export_config_validation_fail_total{field}
- Logs:
  - never log destination secret refs? Actually refs are okay; but safest is to redact any field matching *_ref.

TODOs / decisions needed
1) Workspace-scoped vs tenant-scoped configs
- Security asks: some customers want “everything in tenant” exported. Could be added later as tenant-level export with workspace tags.

2) PATCH vs PUT
- Decide and be consistent across SDKs.

3) Inline secret creation support
- Console UX may want to paste token in the flow. If we allow that, we need a separate secrets API; do not accept raw tokens in audit export endpoints.

4) Filter expressiveness
- Are action wildcards needed? Consider allow action prefix (e.g., "apikey.*"). Risk: validation requires taxonomy service.

5) include_system default
- Align with Marcus/Kevin on what counts as “system” and whether customers expect it.

6) Egress allowlist rules for Dedicated
- Dedicated customers may have private Splunk endpoints. If we disallow private IPs, we need a documented exception mechanism.

7) Backfill semantics in API
- Should backfill be a one-time job triggered on create? If so, should API expose job status? For beta: keep implicit and surface via export lag/status.

8) Status counters shape
- Need to confirm with Logan/Telemetry on acceptable labels + cardinality.

9) Delete behavior
- Soft delete recommended; define retention duration + what status endpoint returns after delete.

References / related
- ADR: Audit export delivery semantics & idempotency (at-least-once; stable event_id)
- ADR: Filtering model (allow/deny + categories/actions predicates)
- Tickets: ENG-5132 (API), ENG-5173 (RBAC), ENG-5160 (filter engine)
- PRs: redwood/pr-28766, redwood/pr-28792

Notes from recent conversations (unstructured)
- Security wants explicit statement in docs/UI: “at-least-once delivery; downstream should deduplicate by event_id”.
- SRE wants a kill switch + auto-pause on max lag (exporter-side), surfaced as status=PAUSED + reason.
- Support has already seen confusion around “missing events” during throttling; status endpoint needs to make lag/backfill visible.

Appendix: Example create request (Splunk)
POST /control-plane/v1/workspaces/w_123/audit-exports
{
  "name": "splunk-prod",
  "enabled": true,
  "destination": {
    "type": "splunk",
    "splunk": {
      "endpoint": "https://http-inputs-acme.splunkcloud.com:8088",
      "hec_token_ref": "secret://workspaces/w_123/splunk_hec_token/versions/3",
      "index": "security",
      "sourcetype": "redwood:audit"
    }
  },
  "filter": {
    "mode": "ALLOW",
    "categories": ["auth","rbac","apikey"],
    "include_system": false
  },
  "backfill": {"on_create": {"enabled": true, "window_hours": 24}},
  "delivery": {"delivery_guarantee": "AT_LEAST_ONCE"}
}

Appendix: Example create request (S3)
{
  "name": "s3-evidence",
  "enabled": true,
  "destination": {
    "type": "s3",
    "s3": {
      "bucket": "acme-redwood-audit",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "prefix": "redwood/audit/",
      "format": "jsonl_gzip",
      "encryption": {"type": "SSE_KMS", "kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/..."},
      "auth": {"mode": "assume_role", "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodAuditExportRole"}
    }
  },
  "filter": {"mode": "DENY", "categories": ["billing"]},
  "backfill": {"on_create": {"enabled": true, "window_hours": 24}}
}
